title: FIG. 03 · Strata, assembled by scroll
summary: Round 2's strata drawing is back, now with three layers. On the homepage the section holds while you scroll: each step drops one layer in, painted red while it is being installed, and opens its row in the list. The last step closes the stack and turns the measurement beside it into one red line running from the bottom layer back to the top.
story: It takes the letter's promise ('one that installs the system, then hands you the keys') and shows, layer by layer, the three things Kelwin installs and how they close into one loop. Then it hands over to the operating principle: a system built for clarity, not for more activity.
motion: This mockup plays once by itself and comes to rest on the finished drawing after about 6 seconds. The heading rises. Layer 01 drops in red and its row opens, then 02, then 03; the red moves to each new layer, and the measurement beside the stack reads '3 layers'. Then the stack closes up. The red fades from the last layer as the measurement line is drawn over in red, from the bottom layer back up into the top one, with a single arrow, and the measurement now reads '1 system'. The ring on the last layer closes at the same moment. The title block changes from Exploded to Installed.

On the homepage the heading scrolls normally. Then the drawing and the list hold the screen for about 1,200px of scrolling. Layer 01 lands as the drawing comes into view, and 02, 03 and the closing land at even steps after that. Scrolling back undoes each step. After the hold the section scrolls on, resting closed. Nothing loops and no dots run.
Clicking a row in the list opens it and brightens that layer's name on the drawing. It never moves the red.
With reduced motion, and on phones, there is no hold: you see the finished drawing. On phones the drawing is cropped to the stack and fills the column, and the list below names the layers.
addressed: 'I really liked the design language of round 2 with the strata assembly kind of structure.' It's back as you approved it: flat 3D layers with each one's job drawn on its face, numbered name tags on the right, the measurement on the left, corner marks, a small title block, and the list beside the drawing that opens one row at a time.

'…where it animates and all that stuff.' The layers still drop in one at a time, the one being installed is painted solid red, and the stack closes up while the measurement changes from '3 layers' to '1 system'. On the homepage this is driven by your scroll: the section holds the screen, and each step lands one layer and opens its row.

'Looks too cluttered.' All of round 3's extras are gone: the loop labels (Capital in, Campaigns run, Knowledge lost, Reset), the ERR stamp, the moving dots, the stacked rings, the Reroute effort and Compounding pipeline labels, the five-step bar and the counter. What remains is one drawing, three names, one measurement and one title block.

'Too hard to understand. Nothing seems clear.' The closed loop is now a single red line. Once the third layer lands, the measurement beside the stack is drawn over in red, from the bottom layer back into the top one, with one arrow, and it reads '1 system'. The row left open beside it says what that return does: 'we retune the system with you each quarter'.

The three layers use your menu's names and one-line descriptions. Each row's 'In practice' line starts with 'We…' and says what Kelwin actually builds in your company, so the section reads as installing, not advising, and stays out of Plurel's demand-and-distribution lane.
notes: LAYOUT: stack X's composition. The head grammar sits on top: label, the two-voice statement, the 48×2 rule and the lede. Below it, 64px down, the drawing sits in a registration frame (cols 1–7, a 640px field plus a 56px caption row) and the ledger sits in cols 9–12; the ledger's top rule lines up with the frame's top marks. One quiet door sits 36px under the ledger. GEOMETRY is generated (work/system-W/gen.mjs writes W.html) in plan coordinates projected to true 30° isometric. Each slab is 212×132 in plan and 12 thick. The installed pitch is 144 and the exploded pitch is 184 (±40 on slabs 01 and 03), so the slab above never covers a face. The inscriptions are CONTOUR text rules for Narrative, a TRACE fork (one signal routed three ways) for Infrastructure, and an ORBIT open ring with a rider for Intelligence; its gap closes at step 4. THE LOOP: the founder asked for both the '1 SYSTEM' bracket and one clean return path with one quiet label. Drawn separately, they read as a box with a line inside it (first render). So they are one element: the bracket's extension lines and dimension line form the exact ⊏ that the red return takes. At step 4 the ticks fade and the ⊏ is plotted in signal red (pathLength plot, 1.1s), from slab 03's left corner, up, into slab 01's left corner, with one 12px open chevron on the riser. The bracket's value, '1 system', is the loop's one quiet label. RED: one place at a time. During steps 1–3 it is the top face of the slab being installed (lifted 8px, inscription in paper). At step 4 the face drains (a 450ms delay, only during the hand-off) as the return draws from its corner. At rest the only red is the return, plus the head's label square and rule. LEDGER: stack X's ledger, rebuilt with three rows: index, nav name, descriptor and toggle. One row is open at a time, and row 03 stays open at rest. Rows not yet installed are quieter, and the row being installed gets a 1px --fg top rule. The rows stay buttons. COPY: everything is verbatim from stack X, system S and the nav, with one exception, the lede. The /about caption ('Capital in, campaigns run, knowledge lost, reset. The loop conserves nothing…') does NOT fit cleanly as the lede: placed straight under 'One closed loop.', 'The loop conserves nothing' reads as if it describes Kelwin's loop, and the broken-loop drawing that gave it context in round 3 is gone. I also tried it as a head note labelled 'The loop most teams run'; that sat directly above the ledger and read as the ledger's heading, so I cut it. The lede is stack X's approved line adapted for three layers, which also avoids repeating the statement: 'Kelwin installs all three in your company, so pipeline becomes a standing output, not a one-time deliverable.' So the STORY §2 ★ caption line is not rendered in this slot; the letter just before already carries 'every quarter starts from zero'. 'In practice' sources: 01 is stack X and system S, 02 is system S, 03 is stack X (chosen over S so all three start with 'We…'). The word 'compound' is not used. PIN: it is not a ScrollTrigger pin. The track is 100vh/zoom + 1200px tall and the stage is position: sticky. The step is read from the track's getBoundingClientRect in rAF and converted to pinned units: steps 1–4 begin at −320, 240, 540 and 840, so step 1 lands as the frame enters, before the pin, and the rest hold from 840 to 1200. Each step is a timed CSS transition triggered when its threshold is crossed (not scrubbed), and crossing back reverses it. The track's margin-top is calc(64px − (100vh/zoom − body height)/2), so the head-to-drawing gap stays at 64px in the flow. On viewports shorter than body + 48px the stage scales the body down. Tested at 1440×900 (zoom 1) and 1280×720 (zoom .889) with no console errors. Only under html.km-home, wide, with motion on, does the script add .is-pinned and .is-live; without them the CSS is the assembled state. On the homepage the section arms itself at script load and plays its own head entrance (an IntersectionObserver on the root with a −6% bottom margin), because the page player waits until 22% of this tall section is visible. STANDALONE: an automatic demo that plays once, with steps at 0.9, 1.9, 2.9 and 3.9s; the red return finishes at about 5.7s. It is not a contact sheet. ROBUSTNESS: tall full-page captures briefly re-evaluate the ≤760px query. So the phone rules hide things with visibility rather than display (display would restart the registration-mark entrance), entrance hooks retire (.is-settled) after 2.6s, and the media-query listener is debounced (it acts only on a change that holds for 250ms). PHONES: no pin. The drawing is cropped to the stack and its return (x 130–610, y 60–580) and scaled to the column (--fs = width/480, capped at 1). The callouts and the bracket value are hidden there; the ledger names the layers. Checked with a freed 390px stage.
